one_liner: Google's per-CPU-cache C/C++ allocator, positioned as a faster-at-scale alternative to glibc malloc, though unquantified in the repo.
what_it_does: TCMalloc is Google's production C/C++ memory allocator, implementing malloc/free/calloc/realloc and C++11-17 operator new/delete including sized and overaligned delete. It is not a header swap: you link it in as your binary's allocator (e.g. Bazel's `malloc` attribute), replacing glibc malloc or the default operator new. It targets multi-threaded, highly parallel server applications rather than single-threaded microbenchmarks.
how_it_is_fast: Fast-path allocation/free happens in a per-CPU cache (default) or per-thread cache (fallback), both lock-free for the common case. Per-CPU mode uses Linux restartable sequences (RSEQ, kernel >=4.18) so a core-local push/pop either completes atomically or is transparently restarted on preemption/migration, avoiding atomic instructions. Cache misses refill from a CentralFreeList/TransferCache middle-end sized by allocatable size-classes, backed by a hugepage-aware page-heap (TEMERAIRE) that cuts TLB pressure and fragmentation versus the legacy pageheap.
when_to_use: Highly parallel, multi-threaded C++ server workloads on Linux x86-64/AArch64 with RSEQ kernel support (>=4.18)
Already building with Bazel and Abseil, or willing to add both as dependencies
Need built-in heap telemetry/sampling (MallocExtension) for fleet-scale memory tracking
Large-fleet deployments where small reductions in pageheap overhead/RAM matter at scale (per the OSDI 2021 TEMERAIRE data)
OK rebuilding from source at or near HEAD rather than linking a stable prebuilt library
when_not_to_use: Non-Linux targets: no documented Windows/macOS support; only Linux is supported, PPC is 'best effort'
Kernels <4.18 or RSEQ disabled: falls back to legacy per-thread caching, losing the main fast-path win
Code that needs std::bad_alloc/exception-based OOM handling: TCMalloc crashes directly on allocation failure instead of throwing
Projects that cannot add Abseil (and Bazel, or the experimental CMake path) as build dependencies
Anything needing dynamic load/unload of the allocator or ABI stability across TCMalloc versions: neither is supported or promised

integration.form: source-drop / static lib (built from source with Bazel; no prebuilt binary, no header-only mode)
integration.dependencies: Abseil (hard dependency, pinned in MODULE.bazel); also pulls in protobuf, re2, bazel_skylib as Bazel deps
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (C11 for C code); gcc 12.1+ or clang 11.0+; Bazel 4.0+ (CMake support experimental)
integration.platforms: Linux x86 and AArch64, little-endian 64-bit, libstdc++/libc++ (PPC best-effort); no Windows/macOS documented
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe allocator; default per-CPU caching (needs Linux RSEQ, kernel >=4.18) or per-thread fallback, both avoiding locks on the fast path (docs/overview.md, docs/rseq.md)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces malloc/operator new via build-system linkage (e.g. Bazel's `malloc` attribute), same C11/C++17 allocation API surface, but does not throw on OOM (crashes instead) and offers no ABI stability

gotchas: No ABI stability: docs/compatibility.md says build from source (ideally HEAD), don't depend on a compiled representation, don't open namespace tcmalloc, don't take the address of its API functions
Allocation failure crashes the process instead of throwing std::bad_alloc, which can surprise code relying on exception-based OOM handling
The RSEQ fast path is fragile in practice: closed issue #292 documents crashes on Linux >=6.19 from RSEQ ABI interaction with glibc's own rseq registration
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick over gperftools' tcmalloc when you want the actively developed successor with per-CPU RSEQ caching and the hugepage-aware TEMERAIRE backend, instead of gperftools' legacy per-thread-only pageheap. Pick mimalloc/jemalloc/snmalloc instead when you want a documented head-to-head number against your baseline in-repo — none of google/tcmalloc's docs quantify it against glibc, std::allocator, or those allocators.
verified_claims_summary: No numeric benchmark of google/tcmalloc vs glibc malloc (or std::allocator/operator new) appears in the repo; overview.md only claims it is 'designed to be more efficient at scale.' The only peer-reviewed numbers found (Hunter, Kennelly et al., OSDI 2021) measure TCMalloc's hugepage-aware TEMERAIRE backend against TCMalloc's own prior legacy pageheap, not glibc: +7.7% RPS / -2.4% RAM (abstract), +5.2% average throughput (Table 1) across 8 Google WSC apps, pageheap overhead 14.3%->10.6% (Fig. 15), fleet IPC +1.2%, and Redis 6.0.9 +0.75%/+0.44% RPS (LLVM -O3, Skylake Xeon, 2000 trials).
status_note: Actively maintained (commits current as of the record date) and Apache-2.0/copyable, but not a drop-in swap: expect to vendor the source, add Abseil, and build with Bazel rather than link a stable prebuilt library.
